original_question: For a finite group G, let the type of G be the function on positive integers whose value at n is the number of solutions of the equation xn = 1 in G. a) Is it true that a group having the same type as a group with trivial solvable radical must also have trivial solvable radical? Note that there are solvable and nonsolvable groups with the same type(see 12.37). b) Is it true that a group having the same type as an almost simple group must be isomorphic to it? This is true for a group having the same type as a simple group, as follows from the affirmative answer to 12.39(in Archive).
target_in_paper: Open problem 21.134(a,b) in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)". The draft is essentially the paper’s own wording, not a broader reformulation of 12.37 or 12.39. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct invariant (“type” as the counting function n ↦ number of solutions of x^n = 1), the two intended subquestions, and the exact contextual remarks used in the paper: the warning that solvable and nonsolvable groups can share a type refers back to 12.37, and the positive statement for simple groups refers back to the solved archive problem 12.39. In substance, it is already very close to problem 21.134 itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the draft should quantify over two finite groups, say G and H, rather than saying only “a group having the same type as a group ...”.

It should explicitly define the type function as t_G(n) = |{x in G : x^n = 1}| for every positive integer n, and state that “having the same type” means t_G(n) = t_H(n) for all n ≥ 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
It should unpack “trivial solvable radical” by naming the solvable radical R(G), so the condition becomes R(G) = 1.

It should define “almost simple” explicitly: there exists a nonabelian finite simple group T such that T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T). The paper gives this standard definition elsewhere. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
In part (b), the pronoun “it” should be replaced by the specific almost simple comparison group to avoid ambiguity.

If the goal is a single sharp stand-alone question, the two parts should be presented as two assertions about the same invariant, with the simple-group case mentioned only as background rather than folded into the main statement. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let t_G : positive integers → positive integers be the type of a finite group G, defined by t_G(n) = |{x in G : x^n = 1}|. Let R(G) denote the solvable radical of G. Determine whether the following assertions are true: (i) if H is a finite group and there exists a finite group G with R(G) = 1 such that t_H(n) = t_G(n) for every positive integer n, then R(H) = 1; and (ii) if G is a finite almost simple group, meaning that T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T) for some nonabelian finite simple group T, and H is a finite group with t_H(n) = t_G(n) for every positive integer n, then H is isomorphic to G.
justification: The draft matches problem 21.134(a,b) almost verbatim, including the two cross-references that identify its precise intent: 12.37 is cited only to note that mere solvability is not determined by type, while 12.39 is cited to explain why the analogous recognition statement is already known when the comparison group is simple. That makes 21.134, not 12.37 or 12.39 themselves, the exact target. The only real refinement needed is to make the quantifiers, notation, and the meaning of “almost simple” fully explicit so that the question stands on its own outside the notebook’s running terminology. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
